episodes.title: The Signals Animals Give Before They Move
episodes.hookPrompt: Before an animal takes a step, what might its posture and attention already be telling us?
episodes.storyQuestion: How can viewers observe behaviour without inventing meaning or disturbing the animal?
episodes.nextEpisodeTease: Next, we look at the role patience can play in predator behaviour.
episodes.researchAndFootageGate: Use verified species-specific sources and original camera footage showing the behaviour discussed. Do not generalise one species' signals to all animals.

episodes.title: Why Predators Wait
episodes.hookPrompt: A wildlife encounter is not always defined by the chase. Sometimes the pause is the story.
episodes.storyQuestion: What can observation, habitat and energy use explain about waiting behaviour in the featured species?
episodes.nextEpisodeTease: Next, we explore what happens when different animals share the same water source.
episodes.researchAndFootageGate: Research the featured species and context. Do not stage, provoke or imply a hunt that the original footage does not show.

episodes.title: The Hidden Rules of the Waterhole
episodes.hookPrompt: A waterhole can bring very different animals into the same frame. What should we notice?
episodes.storyQuestion: How do habitat, timing and species-specific behaviour shape visits to shared water sources?
episodes.nextEpisodeTease: Next, we follow the early learning that helps young animals navigate their environment.
episodes.researchAndFootageGate: Use local ecological research and original recordings. Avoid implying a fixed hierarchy or interaction without evidence.

episodes.title: How Young Animals Learn the Wild
episodes.hookPrompt: The first months of an animal's life can be full of lessons. Which moments can we actually observe?
episodes.storyQuestion: What is known about learning, development and care in the featured species?
episodes.nextEpisodeTease: Next, we explore how wildlife behaves after the light fades.
episodes.researchAndFootageGate: Use verified developmental research and naturally recorded footage. Do not approach nests, dens or dependent young to obtain shots.

episodes.title: Life After Dark
episodes.hookPrompt: When daylight disappears, the wildlife story does not necessarily end. What changes after dark?
episodes.storyQuestion: How do the senses and behaviours of the featured nocturnal or crepuscular species support its activity?
episodes.nextEpisodeTease: Next, we look at the quiet survival value of camouflage.
episodes.researchAndFootageGate: Use footage recorded without disturbing animals and disclose any unusual recording equipment or lighting where relevant. Never fabricate night sounds.

episodes.title: The Quiet Work of Camouflage
episodes.hookPrompt: Sometimes the most remarkable animal in a scene is the one you almost missed.
episodes.storyQuestion: How does camouflage work for the featured species in its actual habitat?
episodes.nextEpisodeTease: Season two will follow a new set of species and habitats.
episodes.researchAndFootageGate: Use species-specific evidence and genuine habitat footage. Do not digitally alter the animal or background in a way that misrepresents the encounter.

episodeStandard.closingCta: Invite viewers to watch the next episode and explore the Nature Frontiers channel.

releaseStatus: No episode is production-ready until original footage, source rights, research, narration, edit, thumbnail, captions and human approval are verified.
